findings.reason: adding s11 to s7's declared waits is what holds the admit service's node until the dispatch can read a section's control.
findings.text: §11 closes with "A section the queue cannot read this from is a section no unattended pass can queue, which is what §7 needs", but `plan-section-depends-on` gives s7 only s3 and s4, so s7 may be dispatched before s11 lands and its pass will meet the same queue-time refusal s11 exists to remove

findings.reason: the half of the endpoint a reader needs in order to fix the section is unmeasured, so the node can close with the weaker behaviour.
findings.text: §11's deliverable requires the refusing case to name "the section and what is missing from it", while the second arm asserts only that it is "refused naming the section", so a refusal that names the section and says nothing about the missing control passes the gate

findings.reason: a worker must either invent a partial marker, which measures its invention, or drop the arm, which changes what the node's gate covers; the plan should name a condition the records can express or withdraw the arm.
findings.text: §12's third arm queues "a section whose run landed a partial node the plan names as partial", but no record carries a partial node: a run's manifest status is `complete`, `blocked` or `failed`, and no landing record distinguishes a landed node as partial (grep over `reckon/crew/` for `partial` returns only log-truncation and atomic-write senses), so the fixture cannot be built from the system the plan describes

findings.reason: the reuse map belongs to the node brief composed from this review, not the plan; fixing the modules in plan text makes a wrong path a plan defect and every other section of this plan names only its evidence path, so the clause is also inconsistent with the plan's own shape.
findings.text: §11 prescribes the implementation: "Write paths: `reckon/crew/dispatch_batch.py`, `reckon/crew/dispatching/requests.py` and the new test" names the modules to extend, and §12 line 100 repeats the form with "`reckon/crew/dispatch_batch.py` and the new test

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/crew/dispatch_batch.py` and `reckon/crew/dispatching/requests.py` exist, the cited head `27ecc8df67` resolves as a commit and is an ancestor of `main`, and `work-scales-to-eighty-across-nodes` with its §1, plus `building-a-plan-queues-all-of-it` §3, all resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §11 requires a refusal naming what is missing from the section but its gate asserts only the section name; §12's third arm rests on a "partial node" no record carries.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both new sections write each arm's log under the run directory, which is durable and re-openable, not a scratchpad or node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, stage names or ticket numbers reach the deliverable text; the run ids in §12's evidence are recorded incident data, not symbol names.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §11 and §12 each carry a "Write paths:" clause naming the source modules to change, which is a method the plan fixes rather than an endpoint.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §11 delivers one read (the section's stated control carried onto the request) and §12 one skip rule, and each gate proves that single deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — `_document` line 23 declares s7's waits as s3 and s4 only, while §11's own closing sentence states §7 needs what §11 delivers.
